assertions_evaluated.text: States that allowed-tools pre-approves tools for the turn that invokes the skill and does not restrict which tools are available, so Write remains callable and would just prompt
assertions_evaluated.evidence: (a) quotes SKILL.md R6: it "only pre-approves the listed tools for the turn that invokes it: it does not restrict which tools are available (every tool stays callable, and an unlisted one falls through to the normal permission prompt)"; adds that Write is not pre-approved so the user's permission settings decide whether it prompts or runs.

assertions_evaluated.text: Classifies the missing Write grant as a tool-completeness finding about prompts, not as a blocked capability or a security boundary
assertions_evaluated.evidence: (b) "The verdict is therefore a grant-completeness finding (missing pre-approval), not a restriction or capability finding"; the finding wording is that report-file creation will raise a permission prompt and "must not say Write is blocked, forbidden or unavailable". The subject marked REQUIRED severity as its own inference from the tool-completeness sub-check.

assertions_evaluated.text: Names disallowed-tools or a permission deny rule as the way to actually restrict a tool
assertions_evaluated.evidence: (c) "Make Write unavailable with `disallowed-tools` or a permission deny rule", citing frontmatter-corrections.md and SKILL.md R6; "Omitting Write from `allowed-tools` is not a restriction."

assertions_evaluated.text: Does not claim the skill is read-only because of its allowed-tools list
assertions_evaluated.evidence: (d) "No. The skill is not read-only because of its allowed-tools list... Any 'read-only' claim resting on `Read Grep` would be wrong."
